title: University of Tokyo Anatomy Department: surviving microscope object plus 1873–1887 preparation, instrument and practical-microscopy archive

principal_upgrade.previous_state: A bounded nineteenth-century Anatomy Department paper trail was known from the Medical Library list: preparation quantities, microscope/instrument indexes, manufactured histology/embryology items, practical microscopy, course diary and microscope records.
principal_upgrade.new_state: The University Museum independently preserves and publicly documents the Medical Faculty's 'No. 1' optical microscope, marked '壹番' and 'T.DENNISROCK & Co LONDON', imported from Britain in the early Meiji period and explicitly used for demonstration during histology practical teaching. This creates a surviving instrument endpoint for the same institutional microscopy system represented by the Medical Library records.

medical_library_archive.system_reading: These records are not a generic departmental archive. Their dates overlap and their administrative functions divide microscopy into preparation quantity, manufactured histology/embryology objects, instrument inventory, practical microscopy and course chronology. Together they form an unusually explicit institutional address system for making, storing and using microscopic preparations.

surviving_object.object: 東京帝国大学医学部 光学顕微鏡 / Medical Faculty optical microscope
surviving_object.historical_designation: 医学部一号機 / Medical Faculty No. 1 microscope
surviving_object.date_state: early Meiji period; precise acquisition date not supplied on the public exhibition record
surviving_object.provenance: Tokyo Imperial University Medical Faculty; current University Museum medical collections
surviving_object.use_statement: The University Museum states that the instrument was used for demonstrations during histology practical teaching.
surviving_object.material_significance: The object converts the Tokyo case from archive-only potential into a surviving instrument-plus-record system.

historical_context.official_university_exhibition_statement: The Meiji medical curriculum introduced anatomy and histology (microscopic anatomy), with both taught in the first year of the medical course.
historical_context.separate_zoology_comparator: University history also documents that in the Zoology Department C. O. Whitman introduced Zeiss microscopes and a microtome around 1879–1880 and taught sectioning, staining and microscopic observation. This is a separate departmental history and should not be collapsed into the Medical Faculty Anatomy archive.

research_mechanism.chain: preparation quantity ledger -> manufactured histology/embryology catalogue -> microscope/instrument index -> microscope records -> practical microscopy -> course diary -> surviving Medical Faculty microscope
research_mechanism.strong_claim: Tokyo preserves both the administrative decomposition of microscopic practice and at least one instrument from the teaching system that practice served.
research_mechanism.best_test: Whether the '壹番' / Medical Faculty No. 1 microscope can be found explicitly in call nos. 119, 122 or 123, with acquisition, location, user or practical-use details.

exact_source_actions.request: Page images of call nos. 119, 122 and 123, beginning with index/opening pages and all entries for microscope no. 1 / 壹番 / Dennisrock or London-made microscopes.
exact_source_actions.upgrade_if_found: Would close surviving object -> historical instrument register at S level.

exact_source_actions.request: Page images of nos. 118, 120 and 121 preserving complete internal order.
exact_source_actions.upgrade_if_found: Would reconstruct preparation manufacture, quantities and practical microscopy as an operational chain rather than merely a list of archival genres.

exact_source_actions.request: Histology course diary no. 110, especially dates overlapping practical microscopy entries in no. 121.
exact_source_actions.upgrade_if_found: Could bind preparation/instrument work to teaching chronology and named exercises.

guards: Do not claim that the surviving Medical Faculty No. 1 microscope is already identified in call nos. 119/122/123; the public archive list gives titles and dates, not entry contents.
Do not use the University Museum's 'early Meiji' wording as a precise acquisition year.
Do not merge the Medical Faculty Anatomy/Histology system with the separate Zoology Department Whitman/Zeiss/microtome history without documentary linkage.
No broad Japan microscopy search is required before the bounded Anatomy Department manuscripts are read.
